title: Crista biopsies of normal, hypoplastic and malignant bone marrow (human) | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Stain: Hematoxylin and eosin. The composition of three slides shows a normal bone marrow section (A),  an aplastic bone marrow (B), and a malignant lymphoma in bone marrow (C). (1) Cristae. (2) Fat tissue or fat cells. (3) Erythrocytes and (4) erythroblasts with dark nuclei.

title: Normal pleiomorph and leukemic monomorph bone marrow smear (human) | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Stain: May-Grnwald-Giemsa (MGG). In normal bone marrow smear (A) a pleimorph or heterogeneous collection of different cell types (A1-7) can be identified, while in the bone marrow smear of a leukemic patient a single type dominates (in this case lymphoid cells, B-1).

title: Pleiomorph normal bone marrow smear (human) | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Stain: May-Grnwald-Giemsa (MGG). The normal bone marrow with pleiomorphism, i.e. contains all stages of the erythroblastic differentiation series (1-5) as well as the stages of the myeloblastic series (6).    (1) Basophilic erythroblast. (2),(3),(4) Polychromatic erythroblasts. (5) Orthochromatic erythroblasts. (6)  Metamyelocytes in different stages. (7) Promonocyte. (8) Reticulocyte.

title: Pleiomorph bone marrow smear (human) | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Stain: May-Grnwald-Giemsa (MGG). Low power view of a normal bone marrow smear. The bone marrow is pleiomorph and contains all cell types such as a large reticulum cells (1) with many granules or lysosomes (phagocytosis); myeloid cells (2); and erythroblasts (3).

title: Normal Vessel in Bone Marrow | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
Iron (Perls) staining of sideroblasts in bone marrow smear (human) | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Stain: Perl's stain for iron (Prussian blue). The intense blue stained hemosiderin in the erythroblasts (1) is visible as siderotic granules (pathologic siderosomes). These pathologic siderosomes are sometimes distributed in a circle around the nucleus (ringed sideroblasts). The myeloid cell types (2) are devoid of these siderotic granules. Normal iron particles are pitted from the cells and reutilized by macrophages in the spleen and reticulum cells in the bone marrow. (3) Proerythroblast with blue granules.

title: Giant neutrophilic metamyelocyte in bone marrow smear (human) | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Stain: May-Grnwald-Giemsa (MGG). (1) Giant neutrophilic metamyelocyte. (2) Normal neutrophilic metamyelocytes. (3) Smudged eosinophilic granulocyte. (4) Orthochromatic erythroblast.

title: Orthochromatic erythroblasts in bone marrow smear (human) | Health Education Assets Library (HEAL)
description: Stain: May-Grnwald-Giemsa (MGG). Two orthochromatic erythroblasts (1) with condensed nuclear chromatin and a transition of cytoplasmic stain towards the color of normal erythrocytes. (2) a segmented neutrophilic granulocyte.
